Calculate risk set and event counts at time points

Source: R/df_counting_helpers.R
calculate_risk_event_counts.Rd

Calculates risk set and event counts for a group at specified time points, with variance estimation. Passed to KM_estimates, these give the Kaplan-Meier estimate only when at_points holds every event time of the group.

Usage

calculate_risk_event_counts(U, D, W, at_points, draws = 0, seedstart = 816951)

Arguments

U

Numeric vector of times for group.

D

Numeric vector of event indicators for group.

W

Numeric vector of weights for group.

at_points

Numeric vector of time points.

draws

Number of draws for variance estimation (default 0).

seedstart

Random seed for draws (default 816951).

Value

List with ybar (risk set counts), nbar (event counts), sig2w_multiplier (variance term: its cumulative sum times \(\hat S(t)^2\) is the variance of the Kaplan-Meier estimate, see KM_estimates).

Details

sig2w_multiplier is, with no weights or all weights equal, the per-time-point Greenwood term \(dN(s) / [Y(s)\{Y(s) - dN(s)\}]\) (0 where \(Y(s) = 0\) or \(Y(s) - dN(s) \le 10^{-10} Y(s)\)). With weights that are not all equal it is the successive differences, along at_points, of \(\sum_i w_i^2 \psi_i(t)^2\) (the robust variance below divided by \(\hat S(t)^2\)), or, when draws > 0, of the variance over draws of \(\sum_i G_i w_i \psi_i(t)\); individual differences may be negative, only their cumulative sum is meaningful.

Variance of the Kaplan-Meier estimate

With no weights, or with all weights equal, the variance of a Kaplan-Meier estimate is Greenwood's formula, and these results are unchanged. When the weights are not all equal it is the robust (infinitesimal-jackknife) variance $$\widehat{Var}[\hat S(t)] = \hat S(t)^2 \sum_i w_i^2 \psi_i(t)^2,$$ $$\psi_i(t) = \frac{D_i 1(U_i \le t)}{Y_w(U_i) - dN_w(U_i)} - \sum_{s \le \min(t, U_i)} \frac{dN_w(s)}{Y_w(s)\{Y_w(s) - dN_w(s)\}},$$ where \(U_i\), \(D_i\) and \(w_i\) are subject \(i\)'s time, event indicator and weight, \(Y_w(s)\) is the weighted number at risk, \(dN_w(s)\) the weighted number of events at \(s\), the sum runs over event times, and a term is 0 where \(Y_w(s) - dN_w(s) \le 10^{-10} Y_w(s)\). It equals the standard error of survival::survfit(weights = w, robust = TRUE) (on the time-fixed data), reduces to Greenwood's formula at equal weights, and does not depend on the scale of the weights. With draws > 0 and unequal weights the variance is instead the variance over resampling draws of \(\sum_i G_i w_i \psi_i(t)\) (standard-normal multipliers \(G_i\)), which estimates the same quantity; resampled curves for weighted data are built from the same per-subject contributions (see resampling_survival). By default the weights are treated as fixed and known. For weights estimated by a logistic propensity model, weight_variance = "estimated" carries their estimation into the standard error (section "Estimated weights" of df_counting). When the weights are extreme (low effective sample size) the standard error can be too small under either option.
